dataset.description: The user studies conducted in task T2.2 will aim to investigate the influence of avatar and environment features on the perception of inappropriate behaviour in 1 to N virtual social interactions. Its objective is to identify and characterise the key factors that modulate how users perceive inappropriate behaviour. The task will delve into various avatar characteristics (e.g., realism, movement, animation, gender, ethnicity, attraction, intimidation, voice, and age) and virtual environment aspects (e.g., size, population density, social setting, and context) while exploring different evaluation methods. Assessment will encompass subjective responses (questionnaires), physiological measures (e.g., eye-tracking, GSR) and behavioural responses, including their impact on proxemics (e.g., stop distance, analysis of the walking trajectory).

format: The experimental studies will produce and use primary (calculated and experimental) data. The primary data includes responses to questionnaires (CSV, XML), performance (CSV, XML), observations (Word, Excel, pdf), images (jpg, tiff, png) and videos (avi, mp4, m4v, mpg).

dataset.preservation_statement: If the dataset is relevant for the research community, it will be freely available either through the associated paper submission (e.g., supplemental materials) or in a dedicated open repository (e.g., zenodo)

security_and_privacy.description: Data will be stored in computers with an encrypted hard drive and require user credentials for logging in.

dataset.title: Study No3 Harassment Prevention through Empathy and Perspective-taking Enhancement

dataset.description: This study focuses on understanding the conditions in which active and efficient bystander behaviour can emerge (size of the group, type of users), and whether tools developed in META-TOO can facilitate it. There will be a series of experiments where the Metaverse users will be a bystander of inappropriate behaviour and their reactions will be analysed, including who, when, and how reacted. Behavioural indicators will be followed by short online questionnaires and semi-structured interviews.

format: CSV, Plain Text files, Audio files

dataset.title: Study No4 Bystander behaviour in the Metaverse

dataset.description: The user studies conducted in task T2.3 will explore interactive methods to enable users either to initiate mitigation strategies when an inappropriate behaviour is detected. Our aim is to enable users to implement pre-emptive actions before an actual moderation can be implemented. The range of potential strategies that can target the key factors identified in task T2.2. This will require design and evaluation of interaction techniques to control such pre-emptive actions. Some potential methods range from modulating the avatar appearance,  dynamically controlling social distances, to completely hiding the avatar of the user having an inappropriate behaviour. One aspect that should be carefully evaluated is the impact that such interactions can have in the local context of each user (e.g., are the changes implemented only in the local context of the user triggering the action? or can/should be enlarged to other local contexts?). Finally, non-intended usages should also be carefully investigated (i.e. the use of pre-emptive actions could generate censorship and potentially a form of virtual harassment on itself).
